chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Al-Halaby, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about buying palm trees, vineyards, and fruits for three years or four years. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.' They say: 'If it does not produce in this year, it will produce in the next. And if you buy it in one year, do not buy it until it ripens. So if you buy it for three years before it ripens, there is no problem.'

And he (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who buys a named fruit crop from a land, but all the fruit of that land perishes. He (peace be upon him) said: 'They disputed regarding that to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). They would mention that dispute. When he saw that they did not cease the dispute, he forbade them from that sale until the fruit ripens, and he did not prohibit it absolutely, but he did that because of their dispute.'
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for buying crops and orchards for multiple years in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the permissibility of purchasing orchards and crops for multiple years, emphasizing that such transactions are valid even if the harvest is not yet ripe, provided the uncertainty is manageable. It highlights the juristic principle of 'al-khal' (avoiding dispute), noting that the Prophet’s prohibition on buying unripened fruit was a pragmatic measure to prevent litigation among people rather than an absolute ban, a nuance preserved by Imam al-Sadiq (AS). This reflects the Shia scholarly approach of distinguishing between the essence of a ruling and its contextual application based on social harmony.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, form Al Halby who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was asked about buying the palm tree and the orchard, and the fruits for the next three years or four years. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it. They are saying that if these do not come out in this year, they would come in the following year, and if it is bought in one year, so do not buy it until it ripens. So if it is bought for three years before the ripening, so there is no problem’.

And he<sup>asws</sup> was asked about the man who buys the fruits of the season from a land, so all of the fruits of that particular land perish. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They had disputed regarding that to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> and they were mentioning that. So when he<sup>saww</sup> saw them that they are not leaving the dispute, he<sup>saww</sup> forbade them from that transaction until the fruits ripened, and he<sup>saww</sup> did no Prohibit it, but he<sup>saww</sup> did that due to the reason of their dispute’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “

Someone once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about buying dates, grapes and fruits of three or four years. He (the Imam) said, ‘There is no offense in it. He (the buyer) can say, “If fruits will not grow this year they will do so next year.” If you buy the fruits of one year only then you must not do so until they are ripe. If you buy them before three years there is no offense in it if the deal takes place before they are ripe.’

Someone asked about buying a certain fruit of a certain land but the fruit of all of that land is ruined. He (the Imam) said, ‘There was dispute about it and it was brought before the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, and they kept speaking about it. When he found out that they do not stop disputing, he prohibited them from such transactions until ripening of fruits and did not make it unlawful. However, he did so because of their disputes.’”
